chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Salih ibn Muhammad, from Yaman al-Tammar, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, for the master of this matter there is a disappearance; one who holds fast to his religion during it is like one who plucks the thorns of al-Qatad with his hand. Then he pondered for a while, then said: Indeed, for the master of this matter there is a disappearance, so let a servant of Allah fear Allah and hold fast to his religion. Do not feel desolate in the path of guidance because of the few who follow it.

key_terms.الْمُمْسِكُ بِدِينِهِ: One who holds fast to his religion
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Command (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam's description of the occultation and holding fast to religion?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the vivid metaphor of placking thorns with bare hands to illustrate the intense spiritual struggle and resilience required to preserve one's faith during the Great Occultation. He further encourages believers not to feel isolated or desolate due to the scarcity of followers, emphasizing that the path of truth is validated by steadfastness rather than numerical majority. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for understanding the psychological and spiritual challenges faced by the Shia community during the prolonged absence of the Imam.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (11) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari from Muhammad bin Eessa from Salih bin Muhammad from Yaman at-Tammar that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“The man of this matter will disappear for a period of time, during which one, who still keeps to his religion, is like one, who lathes thorns of al-Qatad with his bare hand. Which of you can grasp at the thorns of al-Qatad?” Then he pondered for a while and said: “The man of this matter will disappear for a time so people are to fear Allah and to keep to their faith.” The same was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya’qoob al-Kulayni from Muhammad bin Yahya and al-Hasan bin Muhammad from Ja’far bin Muhammad al-Kufi from al-Hasan bin Muhammad as-Sayrafi from Salih bin Khalid from Yaman at-Tammar. Who is this one, who will disappear, but the expected Imam? Who is this one, whose birth and early life most of people will doubt? Who is this one, whom people will be indifferent to and will not believe in his rising nor in his existence even? It is he, whom the infallibles imam (as) have mentioned and described his loyal believers during his disappearance as ones, who grasp at the thorns of al-Qatad with bare hands. It is this little sincere group that is distinguished from the great masses of people, whose fancies have taken them too far away and whose hearts have become too narrow to bear the truth and its bitterness. They find themselves unable to believe in the existence of the Imam while his person is absent and his disappearance has lasted long. Only the little group has believed and kept on believing in the expected Imam (as) following, by that, the saying of Amirul Mo’mineen (as): “Do not feel desolate in the way of guidance when its followers are very few!”
